summary: US Central Command conducted a five-hour strike wave against Iranian facilities at Bushehr, Kharg Island, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas to degrade anti-shipping capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran responded with missile attacks on two UAE tankers in the Strait of Hormuz within Omani territorial waters, killing one Indian crew member and injuring eight others, four seriously. European aviation authorities warned airlines to avoid airspace over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and the Persian Gulf, while Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi plans a visit to Tehran next week.
key_points: US airstrikes hit Iranian facilities across Bushehr, Kish, Kharg, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas in a five-hour operation. (Source: @New_security8200/202556)
Iranian missiles struck two UAE tankers in the Strait of Hormuz (Omani waters), killing one crew member and injuring eight. (Source: @New_security8200/202551)
European aviation agency warned airlines to avoid airspace over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and the Persian Gulf. (Source: @lelotsenzura/93577)
Iran's Hormuz Strait Management reported over 200 non-Iranian ships coordinated transit in three weeks post-MoU before recent escalation. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/377276)
Israeli settlers including four minors crossed into Lebanon near Ghajar, were intercepted and returned by IDF. (Source: @manniefabian/58787)
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi intends to visit Tehran next week at President Pezeshkian's invitation. (Source: @naya_foriraq/82954)
Trump stated the US has "eyes on" Iran's Fordow mountain facility and called it a "good possible target." (Source: @inon_yttach/9442)
Explosions reported at Kish island port and Chamran base, with five missiles hitting the area. (Source: @mamlekate/103884)

points: US Central Command concluded a five-hour strike cycle targeting Iranian facilities at Bushehr, Kharg Island, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas explicitly aimed at degrading Iran's capacity to attack civilian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: @New_security8200/202556)

Multiple explosions rocked Bushehr throughout the night, including the airport, naval training base, and industrial zones, with witnesses reporting at least 11 consecutive blasts and damage to a large refrigerated container stored since the Iran-Iraq war. (Source: @VahidOnline/77049, @rodast_omiddana/76108)
Kish island port and the Chamran base were struck by five missiles around 00:40 local time, according to local reports. (Source: @mamlekate/103884)

Iran's Hormuz Strait Management stated that over 200 non-Iranian vessels coordinated transit and obtained passage permits and insurance during the three-week period following the Islamabad MoU before recent US escalation. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/377276)
A US airstrike in northern Hormozgan Province killed family members of an Iranian park ranger, per Iranian officials. (Source: @presstv/198668)

The strategic Aq Tappeh Khan railway bridge in Golestan Province, a vital link on the China-Russia-Iran corridor via Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan, was rebuilt in under a week after US strike damage. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/377285, @asafroz/51424)
Air defense activity was observed in East Azerbaijan Province, and explosions were reported in Saravan, Sistan and Baluchestan Province. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/4967, @shin_persian/7812)

A group of Israeli settlers, comprising one adult and four minors affiliated with the Uri Tzafon movement, crossed several meters into Lebanon near Ghajar before being intercepted and escorted back to Israel by IDF forces. (Source: @manniefabian/58787)

Several Israeli civilians attempted to cross the border into Syria in the southern Golan Heights but were stopped and detained by IDF troops, then handed to Israeli police. (Source: @inon_yttach/9439)
Prime Minister Netanyahu warned Iranian leaders not to expect a repeat of previous confrontations, stating the next response would be "different - much more powerful." (Source: @N12chat/217389)

Defense Minister Israel Katz submitted a pardon request for Elor Azaria, a former soldier convicted of killing an incapacitated Palestinian attacker in 2016, ahead of Likud primaries. (Source: @amitsegal/63036, @manniefabian/58786)
An explosion was heard in central areas of the occupied territories, though details on origin remain unspecified. (Source: @SharghDaily/171889)
A blast operation targeted the surroundings of Egyptian towers in northern Gaza. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/377284)
Artillery shelling was reported in the Shebaa Farms area. (Source: @redlinkleb/31285)
A signal jamming or communications blackout alert was issued for Lebanon at maximum alert level. (Source: @redlinkleb/31261)
Israeli settlers briefly crossed the border near Ghajar before being returned by the IDF. (Source: @manniefabian/58787)
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi plans to visit Tehran next week in response to an invitation from Iranian President Pezeshkian. (Source: @naya_foriraq/82954)
A fire broke out at Basra International Airport in southern Iraq. (Source: @SharghDaily/171879)
Explosions were reported in Jordan. (Source: @shin_persian/7816)
Israeli civilians attempted to cross into Syria from the southern Golan but were intercepted. (Source: @inon_yttach/9439)

Iranian missiles struck two UAE tankers in the southern shipping lane of the Strait of Hormuz within Omani territorial waters, killing one Indian crew member, injuring eight (four critically), and causing fires on both vessels. (Source: @New_security8200/202551)
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency warned airlines to avoid the airspace of Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and the Persian Gulf. (Source: @lelotsenzura/93577)
Reports indicate Iranian fire directed at a US base in Kuwait. (Source: @lelotsenzura/93576)
Explosions were reported in Manama, Bahrain. (Source: @New_security8200/202554)
Saudi Arabia is reportedly preparing for a potential US ground war against Iran, with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman preemptively striking Houthis to shape conditions. (Source: @kianmeli1/89038)
The targeted UAE tankers are among the world's largest. (Source: @kianmeli1/89035)

sections.threat_assessment: The simultaneous US strikes on Iranian coastal defense nodes and Iranian missile attacks on UAE shipping in the Strait of Hormuz indicate a dangerous escalation cycle where both sides are targeting economic and military infrastructure. The European aviation ban over Gulf airspace reflects credible concern for civilian aviation safety amid active missile exchanges. Iran's rapid reconstruction of the Aq Tappeh Khan railway bridge demonstrates resilient logistics, while Trump's explicit threat against Fordow raises the prospect of strikes on deeply buried nuclear facilities. The involvement of non-state actors like the Uri Tzafon settlers crossing into Lebanon adds an unpredictable dimension to the northern front.
sections.regional_response: Iraq's Prime Minister al-Zaidi's planned Tehran visit signals Baghdad's attempt to mediate or align with Iran amid US-Iran hostilities. Saudi Arabia's reported preemptive strikes on Houthis and preparation for US ground operations suggest Riyadh anticipates a wider conflict. The UAE's tankers being targeted despite their size indicates Iranian willingness to escalate against Gulf energy infrastructure. European aviation warnings show international recognition of the threat to civilian air traffic. Lebanon's signal blackout and artillery fire in Shebaa Farms point to heightened readiness along the Israeli-Lebanese border.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Islamabad MoU's brief de-escalation window allowed Iran to clear oil inventories and coordinate over 200 non-Iranian ship transits, mitigating near-term economic pressure from the renewed US naval blockade. The rapid repair of the Aq Tappeh Khan bridge underscores the strategic priority of the China-Russia-Iran land corridor. Reports of explosions in Saravan, Jordan, and Basra suggest possible spillover or covert operations beyond the main Iran-US axis. The IDF's interception of Israeli civilians attempting to enter Syria and Lebanon reflects concern over unauthorized provocations that could trigger broader clashes.
